newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear in talks ahead of union contract expiry.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear in talks ahead of union contract expiry.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co., the nation's largest tiremaker, said Thursday it was in talks with the United Steelworkers union prior to the Saturday midnight EDT expiration of the contract covering 12,000 of its 91,000 workers.
Both sides agreed to a news blackout when negotiations on a new three-year contract began about two months ago. Talks continued this week at a Cincinnati hotel.
Goodyear, which has a 16 percent stake of the U.S. tire market, is the union's target in pattern bargaining with the industry, Steelworkers union spokesman Curt Brown said.

Besides the traditional issues of wages and benefits, one issue likely to be under discussion was the union's desire to have the various contracts covering Goodyear's 20,000 union workers expire at the same time.
"We're going to either have an agreement, continue the current contract if we're close, or we'll strike," Brown said.
Neither the union nor Goodyear spokesman Fred Haymond would offer any clues about progress in the negotiations.
Saul Ludwig, an analyst at McDonald & Co., said, "I would say congratulations to them for keeping the negotiations quiet."
The 12,000 union employees covered by the expiring master contract work at nine of the global tire maker's 45 U.S. facilities.
One sore point for Goodyear's U.S. workers, which they have in common with automotive and other workers, is the exporting of jobs to countries where labour costs are cheaper.

Brown said the union was irritated by a statement made at the company's annual meeting this week by Goodyear Chairman Samir Gibara that 200 jobs would move to Chile from Akron as the company shifted production of bias-ply racing tires there.
Although pattern bargaining was in effect, union workers at Goodyear's largest competitor, Bridgestone Corp., have a contract that extends for another three years.
That contract for Bridgestone/Firestone workers grew out of a lengthy and bitter 1994 strike during which the company used replacement workers and imported tires.

The long strike sapped the United Rubber Workers' strike fund, and the union subsequently joined the steelworkers to form a 740,000-member union. Goodyear is the largest single employer of the Steelworkers' membership, Brown said.
Goodyear's stock was up 62.5 cents at $52.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
